paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this one. Jeremiah doesn't just say Babylon will fall. He writes it all on a single scroll and sends it to Babylon with Seraiah, to be read aloud right there in the city (Jeremiah 51:60-61). That's how sure God's word is. You don't whisper a promise like that. You hand it to the quartermaster and let it travel.

Then comes the stone. Seraiah ties it to the scroll, throws it into the Euphrates, and says, "In the same way Babylon will sink and never rise again…" (Jeremiah 51:64). The scroll is a picture of what God has promised, and the promise was already settled before any of it happened. Nothing the mightiest empire could build was going to outlast what the LORD had said. I think that should settle something in you, baker, because the same God who stands behind this word stands behind all of His words.

So here's the takeaway to carry out of my bakery. When the LORD says something, you can count on it, even when the world around you looks like it's built to last forever. Read His word, trust His word, and let it steady you when things look big and loud. And the passage ends quiet as can be: "Here end the words of Jeremiah." (Jeremiah 51:64). His words are done, but what God promised still stands.
